advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the _shadow() call in bridge_projects_set/remove OUT of the write_lock block (before it) so its ConfigError fails fast before the lock and is not swallowed by `except ValueError`/`except KeyError`.
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:141: `with lock.write_lock(tracker):`
src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:142: `_shadow(repo_root, "lib.bridge_projects_set")`
src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:144: `except ValueError as exc:` then `raise _invalid_bridge(str(exc)) from exc`
_config_coercion.py:20: `class ConfigError(ValueError):` — so a shadow ConfigError is a ValueError and is caught here
Ticket AC5: 'Malformed selected config raises the typed config error before instrumented lock ... effects' — but the lock is already held when _shadow runs
advisory.finding: In bridge_projects_set and bridge_projects_remove the shadow snapshot is composed INSIDE the write lock, and because ConfigError subclasses ValueError the surrounding `except ValueError`/`except KeyError` catches a malformed-config ConfigError and mis-maps it to _invalid_bridge (returncode 2, 'invalid bridge' message).
advisory.suggested_fix: Call `_shadow(repo_root, "lib.bridge_projects_set")` before entering `with lock.write_lock(tracker):` (mirroring the other lib ops which call _shadow before any lock).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the reconciler shadow boundary should let ConfigError propagate (matching the other surfaces' fail-fast) or document why the reconciler intentionally swallows it.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:628: `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — the compatibility boundary must never break on shadow`
src/rebar/_operation_config.py:245: `except ConfigError:\n        raise` — emit_shadow_snapshot deliberately propagates ConfigError
Ticket description: 'Malformed config fails fast before effects' is a global rule; the reconciler wrapper suppresses it
advisory.finding: The reconciler shadow boundary swallows every exception including ConfigError, so malformed selected config does NOT fail fast for the direct `python -m rebar_reconciler` surface, diverging from the fail-fast contract honored by CLI/lib/MCP where emit_shadow_snapshot re-raises ConfigError.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Compose the CLI shadow snapshot after the subcommand's --root is known (or pass the resolved root) so it reflects the operation's actual repository root.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:546: `emit_shadow_snapshot(surface="cli")` — no repo_root passed
_operation_config.py:211: `root = _config_sources.repo_root(repo_root)` resolves cwd/REBAR_ROOT when repo_root is None

Subcommand `--root` (e.g. `config --root

`) is parsed later during dispatch, after this call
Ticket AC1 expects the CLI-composed snapshot to reflect the same five-layer inputs (including root) as the other surfaces
advisory.finding: The CLI composes the shadow snapshot with no repo_root (emit_shadow_snapshot(surface='cli')), resolving against ambient cwd/REBAR_ROOT before the subcommand's `--root` is parsed, so the CLI snapshot can reflect a different root than the operation actually targets and its fail-fast fires on unrelated ambient config rather than the operation's config.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drive the Python (_lib_ops._shadow), MCP (_mcp_reads/_mcp_writes/_mcp_llm._shadow), and reconciler (_emit_operation_shadow) surfaces through their real entry points in the AC1 equivalence test rather than calling compose_operation_snapshot() directly three times.
evidence: py_snap = compose_operation_snapshot(repo_root=str(p), cli_overrides=overrides)
mcp_snap = compose_operation_snapshot(repo_root=str(p), cli_overrides=overrides)
reconc_snap = compose_operation_snapshot(repo_root=str(p), cli_overrides=overrides)
for other in (mcp_snap, reconc_snap): assert other.fingerprint() == py_snap.fingerprint()

The ticket AC1 requires equivalence 'through CLI, Python, MCP, and the direct reconciler entry point' — the diff wires _lib_ops._shadow, _mcp_reads/_mcp_writes/_mcp_llm._shadow, and _engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__._emit_operation_shadow, none of which this test invokes.
advisory.finding: test_surfaces_compose_equivalent_snapshot (AC1) does not exercise the real per-surface adapters for the Python, MCP, and reconciler surfaces: it calls compose_operation_snapshot(repo_root=str(p), cli_overrides=overrides) three times with identical arguments and asserts the three results are equal. Comparing the same pure function's output to itself is regression-blind — a bug where _lib_ops._shadow / _mcp_reads._shadow / _emit_operation_shadow passes the wrong repo_root, cli_overrides, or surface into the composer would still pass this test. Only the CLI arm invokes a real entry point (rebar._cli.main).
scenarios: An adapter (e.g. the reconciler _emit_operation_shadow) is refactored to drop or mis-map repo_root; the surfaces silently diverge but the test stays green.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that emit_shadow_snapshot returns None and composes nothing when REBAR_OPERATION_SNAPSHOT_SHADOW is set to a canonical false spelling, exercised through the real composition boundary.
evidence: search of tests/ for 'emit_shadow_snapshot' returns (no matches)
search of tests/ for 'REBAR_OPERATION_SNAPSHOT_SHADOW' returns (no matches)
emit_shadow_snapshot body: 'if not shadow_enabled(): return None' then compose/log — the guard branch is never exercised by a test
Ticket Testing: 'The default-enabled and explicit-disabled switch cases prove the compatibility behavior through the real composition boundary.'
advisory.finding: emit_shadow_snapshot() — the function actually threaded into all six surfaces by this diff — has no direct test, and the shadow-disabled kill-switch path is untested end to end. The unit suite only asserts shadow_enabled() returns True/False for spellings; no test asserts that emit_shadow_snapshot returns None (and composes nothing) when REBAR_OPERATION_SNAPSHOT_SHADOW is a false spelling, nor that any wired surface honors the switch. The ticket's Testing plan and AC7 require the explicit-disabled switch case to be proven 'through the real composition boundary.'
scenarios: A regression makes emit_shadow_snapshot compose (and raise ConfigError) even when the kill-switch is set to false, defeating the documented rollback; no test catches it.

The caught-non-config-fault branch (return None + redacted warning) inside emit_shadow_snapshot is only observed indirectly via the CLI fingerprint-boom test; a regression in the warning redaction/return there is largely uncovered at the unit level.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a relative-path config value in the snapshot resolves against the independently selected repo_root, not ambient cwd.
evidence: Ticket AC3: 'Explicit input wins each pairwise precedence case, and relative paths resolve against the independently selected repository root.'
test file covers precedence pairs (test_precedence_*) and root selection (test_explicit_root_A_used_not_ambient_root_B) but no test uses a relative path value and checks its resolution base.
advisory.finding: AC3's explicitly-specified behavior 'a winning relative path is interpreted against the independently selected repository root' has no test. The precedence and root-A-vs-ambient-B cases are covered, but no test sets a relative-path config value and asserts it resolves against the selected repo_root.
scenarios: A relative-path config key is resolved against cwd instead of the selected repo_root; no snapshot test detects the regression.
